# TruckSizer: Visual Moving Truck Cargo Volume & Vehicle Sizing Engine
> High-performance 2.5D isometric moving truck fit planner, spatial volumetric modeling tool, and commercial logistics rate comparison engine.

- [Official Website](https://www.trucksizer.com)
- [Full LLM Documentation](https://www.trucksizer.com/llms-full.txt)

## Project Summary
TruckSizer models real-world cargo volume inside standard US rental moving trucks (10ft, 12ft, 15ft, 16ft, 20ft, 26ft). It combines an interactive 2.5D isometric HTML5 canvas cross-section with an automated packing heuristic and dynamic box estimator to verify whether a household inventory or individual furniture item fits safely before moving day.

## Core Logistics Mechanics & Mathematical Formulas

### 1. Mandatory 18% Real-World Packing Inefficiency Buffer
Raw cubic footage advertised by rental providers (U-Haul, Budget, Penske) represents 100% water-tight liquid capacity. Because furniture has irregular silhouettes, tapered cushions, wheel wells, and structural gaps, 100% space utilization is physically impossible.
- Usable Capacity (cu ft) = Interior Gross Volume (cu ft) × 0.82
- Fill Percentage (%) = (∑ Item Volume Cu Ft / Usable Capacity Cu Ft) × 100
- Capacity Thresholds:
  - 0% to 70%: Optimal Fit (Safe, comfortable loading).
  - 71% to 85%: Caution (Tight fit; requires professional ceiling-height stacking).
  - > 85%: Critical (Over capacity; upgrade to next vehicle size recommended).

### 2. Commercial Rental Truck Specifications (US Standard Fleet)
- 10-ft Truck: 119″L × 76″W × 74″H | 402 cu ft Gross (329 cu ft Usable) | Max Payload: 2,810 lbs | No cab shelf | Suitable for: Studio / Dormitory
- 12-ft Truck: 144″L × 78″W × 78″H | 507 cu ft Gross (416 cu ft Usable) | Max Payload: 3,100 lbs | Low deck, no attic | Suitable for: 1-Bedroom Small
- 15-ft Truck: 180″L × 92″W × 86″H | 764 cu ft Gross (626 cu ft Usable) | Max Payload: 6,385 lbs | Mom's Attic: 36″L × 76″W × 30″H | Suitable for: 1-2 Bedroom Apartment
- 16-ft Truck: 192″L × 90″W × 86″H | 860 cu ft Gross (705 cu ft Usable) | Max Payload: 4,300 lbs | Flat floor deck | Suitable for: 2-Bedroom Apartment
- 20-ft Truck: 240″L × 92″W × 86″H | 1,016 cu ft Gross (833 cu ft Usable) | Max Payload: 5,700 lbs | Mom's Attic: 36″L × 76″W × 30″H | Suitable for: 2-3 Bedroom Home
- 26-ft Truck: 312″L × 98″W × 99″H | 1,682 cu ft Gross (1,379 cu ft Usable) | Max Payload: 9,010 lbs | Mom's Attic: 36″L × 82″W × 32″H | Suitable for: 4+ Bedroom House

### 3. Box Estimation Formula
Total Boxes = ((Bedrooms × 20) + (Occupants × 10)) × Density Multiplier
- Density Multipliers: Minimalist = 0.8x, Standard = 1.0x, Packrat = 1.35x
- Box Size Distribution:
  - Small (1.5 cu ft, books/cans): 30% of total
  - Medium (3.0 cu ft, kitchen/clothes): 45% of total
  - Large (4.5 cu ft, linens/pillows): 15% of total
  - Wardrobe (16.0 cu ft, hanging garments): Bedrooms × 2 (minimum 2)

### 4. 5-Phase Commercial Loading Sequence
1. Phase 1 (Side Walls, Z = 0): Mattresses, box springs, dining tabletops stood on edge along driver-side rail.
2. Phase 2 (Front Bulkhead, X = 0): Sofas stood vertically; heavy solid dressers flat on floor deck (low center of gravity).
3. Phase 3 (Floor Deck, Y = 0): Desks, nightstands, and heavy machinery flat on open deck coordinates.
4. Phase 4 (Mom's Attic, Y > 50″): Fragile electronics, china, and lightweight wardrobe boxes in cab shelf.
5. Phase 5 (Dense Box Tiers): Standardized vertical box columns floor-to-ceiling (heavy large boxes on bottom).
